chunks: 5539 - Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Khālid al-Ṭawīl, who said:

My father called me when death approached him and said: “O my son, take charge of your younger brothers’ wealth, invest it, take half of the profit, and give them the other half; and there is no liability upon you.”
Then, after my father’s death, my father’s umm walad brought me before Ibn Abī Laylā and said: “This man is consuming the wealth of my children.”

He said: So I related to him what my father had instructed me to do. Ibn Abī Laylā said: “If your father instructed you with something invalid, I will not permit it.” Then Ibn Abī Laylā had me affirm that if I put it into use, then I would be liable for it.

Then afterward I entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and related my story to him. Then I said to him: “What do you think?” He said: “As for the statement of Ibn Abī Laylā, I cannot overturn it; but as for what is between you and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is no liability upon you.”

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدِ: a concubine who bore her master a child
key_terms.إِخْوَتِكَ: your brothers; specifically the younger dependent siblings
key_terms.ضَمَانٌ: legal or financial liability for loss or compensation
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; honorific description of Allah
key_terms.مَالَ: property or wealth being placed under management
key_terms.ٱلرِّبْحِ: profit generated from investing or working with the wealth
key_terms.ٱلْبَاطِلِ: that which is invalid or without legal standing
key_terms.ٱلْوَفَاةُ: death; the father’s final illness and approaching death

ai.seo_question: Is a guardian liable for losses when investing the wealth of minor children with permission from the deceased father?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns a dying father appointing his son to manage the wealth of his minor brothers and to share the profit from investing it. When the matter was challenged before a judge, Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام distinguished between the judge’s enforceable ruling and the son’s actual accountability before Allah, affirming that he was not liable in the latter sense.
